# BibTeX lint rules

Each rule has an ID used by diagnostics, `select`/`ignore`, and suppression comments.
These settings also apply to the [LaTeX rules](linter-rules.md). See
[configuration](configuration.md#lint) for rule selection.

Each section states the rule's default. `tex-ls lint --fix` applies safe fixes;
`--unsafe-fixes` also permits changes to typeset output. Examples show diagnostics
and safe fixes generated by the linter.


## `duplicate-key`

Report repeated citation keys within a bibliography or across one root's bibliography resources and manual `\bibitem` definitions. Keys are compared case-insensitively. Every definition after the first is reported. No fix is offered because the author must choose which entry to rename or remove.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

The same cite key defined by two entries:

```bib
@misc{knuth84, title = {Draft}}
@book{knuth84, title = {Book}}
```

```text
warning: duplicate-key
 --> references.bib:2:7
  |
2 | @book{knuth84, title = {Book}}
  |       ^^^^^^^ cite key `knuth84` is defined more than once
```

## `deprecated-suppression-syntax`

Flag the retired `@comment{tex-ls-ignore <rule>}` and `@comment{tex-ls-ignore-file [<rule>]}` suppression spellings, which remain accepted for compatibility but are no longer documented. The Safe autofix rewrites only the family and verb to `tex-ls-lint skip` or `tex-ls-lint skip-file`; the selector, reason, delimiters, and remaining entry text stay byte-for-byte unchanged. This meta diagnostic is not silenced by the retired directive it reports; use `[lint].ignore` to disable the rule deliberately.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

A retired suppression directive in a structured comment:

```bib
@comment{tex-ls-ignore unused-string: intentional}
@string{x = {X}}
```

```text
warning: deprecated-suppression-syntax
 --> references.bib:1:10
  |
1 | @comment{tex-ls-ignore unused-string: intentional}
  |          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ retired suppression syntax; use `@comment{tex-ls-lint skip …}` instead
```

After applying the fix:

```bib
@comment{tex-ls-lint skip unused-string: intentional}
@string{x = {X}}
```

## `inert-suppression`

Report `skip` without a following entry, `on` without `off`, and format-suppression directives, which BibTeX formatting does not support. Also report an unclosed `off`, which suppresses through the end of the file. No fix is offered because the intended boundary is unknown. Suppression comments cannot hide this finding; use `[lint].ignore` to disable it.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

BibTeX recognizes the directive grammar, but its formatter has no suppression mechanism:

```bib
@comment{tex-ls-format skip-file: preserve this file}
@book{key}
```

```text
warning: inert-suppression
 --> references.bib:1:1
  |
1 | @comment{tex-ls-format skip-file: preserve this file}
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the BibTeX formatter does not support format suppression, so this directive does nothing
```

## `missing-required-field`

Report fields required by the biblatex entry type but missing from an entry. Alternatives such as `date` or `year` and aliases such as `journal` for `journaltitle` are accepted. Unknown entry types are excluded. No fix can supply the missing content.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

An `@article` without its required `journaltitle`:

```bib
@article{doe2020,
  author = {Doe, Jane},
  title  = {A study},
  year   = 2020
}
```

```text
warning: missing-required-field
 --> references.bib:1:10
  |
1 | @article{doe2020,
  |          ^^^^^^^ entry `article` is missing required field `journaltitle`
```

## `unknown-field`

Report fields not listed for a known entry type and without global field metadata. BibLaTeX ignores unknown fields. Unknown entry types are excluded, and no fix is offered because deleting a field would discard data.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

A typo'd field name (`pubisher` for `publisher`):

```bib
@book{turing50,
  author   = {Turing, Alan},
  title    = {A book},
  pubisher = {Elsevier},
  year     = 1950
}
```

```text
warning: unknown-field
 --> references.bib:4:3
  |
4 |   pubisher = {Elsevier},
  |   ^^^^^^^^ unknown field `pubisher` on `book` entry
```

## `empty-field`

Flag a field whose value is empty or whitespace-only (`title = {}`, `note = ""`). An empty field carries no data, and some styles still emit punctuation around it. The safe autofix deletes the field along with its separating comma.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

An empty `note` left behind by an edit:

```bib
@misc{knuth84,
  title = {Draft},
  note  = {}
}
```

```text
warning: empty-field
 --> references.bib:3:3
  |
3 |   note  = {}
  |   ^^^^^^^^^^ field `note` is empty
```

After applying the fix:

```bib
@misc{knuth84,
  title = {Draft}
}
```

## `duplicate-field`

Report repeated field names within an entry, compared case-insensitively. Every occurrence after the first is reported. A safe fix removes a repeated value when it matches the retained value byte for byte. Different values receive no fix because the retained occurrence depends on the bibliography engine.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

Two `note` fields with identical values -- deleting the redundant copy is safe:

```bib
@misc{knuth84,
  note = {Draft},
  note = {Draft}
}
```

```text
warning: duplicate-field
 --> references.bib:3:3
  |
3 |   note = {Draft}
  |   ^^^^ duplicate field `note` on `misc` entry
```

After applying the fix:

```bib
@misc{knuth84,
  note = {Draft}
}
```

Differing values are report-only (which copy the engine keeps is style-dependent, so dropping either would change semantics):

```bib
@misc{knuth84,
  note = {First draft},
  note = {Second draft}
}
```

```text
warning: duplicate-field
 --> references.bib:3:3
  |
3 |   note = {Second draft}
  |   ^^^^ duplicate field `note` on `misc` entry
```

## `unused-string`

Report an `@string` macro that no field in the file references. Cross-file string resolution is not supported, so another bibliography may still use the macro. No automatic fix is offered.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

A defined macro no field value references:

```bib
@string{cup = {Cambridge University Press}}
@book{turing50, title = {Draft}, publisher = {Springer}}
```

```text
warning: unused-string
 --> references.bib:1:9
  |
1 | @string{cup = {Cambridge University Press}}
  |         ^^^ `@string` macro `cup` is defined but never used
```

## `unused-entry`

Hint when a bibliography entry is unused in every complete, rooted document that loads this file. Disabled by default for shared libraries. Wildcard citations count as use; incomplete or unrooted namespaces produce no hints.

This rule is **disabled by default**; enable it with `select`.

A complete document loads this resource but cites no entries:

```bib
@misc{unused, title = {Draft}}
```

```text
help: unused-entry
 --> references.bib:1:7
  |
1 | @misc{unused, title = {Draft}}
  |       ^^^^^^ bibliography entry `unused` is unused in its complete document roots
```

## `undefined-string`

Report a string macro with no definition in the file. The twelve month macros `jan` through `dec` are predefined. Cross-file string resolution is not supported, so a definition in another bibliography may produce a false positive. No automatic fix is offered.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

A typo'd macro name (`cpu` for `cup`):

```bib
@string{cup = {Cambridge University Press}}
@book{turing50, title = {Draft}, publisher = cpu}
```

```text
warning: undefined-string
 --> references.bib:2:46
  |
2 | @book{turing50, title = {Draft}, publisher = cpu}
  |                                              ^^^ `@string` macro `cpu` is used but never defined
```

## `title-capitalization`

Report unprotected acronyms and mid-word capitals in title fields. Bibliography styles may lowercase them unless braces protect the spelling, as in `{DNA}`. The rule detects consecutive capitals and names such as `iPhone`. It excludes ordinary title case, names such as `McDonald`, mixed-case words such as `LaTeX`, and already braced text. No fix is offered because the author must choose which spelling to preserve.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

An unprotected acronym a title-lowercasing style would render as `dna`:

```bib
@article{watson53, title = {Molecular structure of DNA}}
```

```text
warning: title-capitalization
 --> references.bib:1:52
  |
1 | @article{watson53, title = {Molecular structure of DNA}}
  |                                                    ^^^ unprotected capitals `DNA` in `title`; wrap in braces (`{DNA}`) to keep case under title-lowercasing styles
```

## `encoding-hints`

Report non-ASCII field text as a hint. Accented text is valid when the file encoding and TeX toolchain agree. Check the encoding or use an escape such as `\'e` for `é`. No fix is offered because the choice depends on the project's toolchain.

This rule is **enabled by default**.

An accented name entered as raw UTF-8:

```bib
@article{erdos47, author = {Erdős, Paul}}
```

```text
help: encoding-hints
 --> references.bib:1:32
  |
1 | @article{erdos47, author = {Erdős, Paul}}
  |                                ^ non-ASCII text `ő`; ensure the file is UTF-8 and the document loads an input encoding (inputenc/fontspec), or use a LaTeX escape
```

## Suppression

BibTeX has no line-comment token. Suppression directives use a structured
`@comment` entry instead of the LaTeX `%` directive. A plain directive
suppresses one rule on the **next entry**:

```bib
@comment{tex-ls-lint skip missing-required-field: publisher long gone}
@book{oldbook, title = {An Orphaned Book}}
```

As in LaTeX, `off` and `on` delimit a
region of entries, and `skip-file` covers the whole file wherever it sits:

```bib
@comment{tex-ls-lint off missing-required-field: imported, incomplete by design}
@book{oldbook, title = {An Orphaned Book}}
@comment{tex-ls-lint on missing-required-field}
```

Naming the `<id>` is optional; leaving it out suppresses every rule over that
same span. Parse diagnostics (rule id `parse`) are never suppressed.
